page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.16-128 is an Arm-based compute instance built on Ampere Altra processors. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped directly to 16 physical cores operating at a consistent 3.0 GHz frequency, with exactly one thread per core. This architecture avoids execution variations associated with simultaneous multithreading. Backing these cores is 128 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU.

In terms of secondary hardware components, this configuration lacks integrated local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent disk operations require network-attached block volumes. It also contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs, directing all compute routines strictly to the 16 Ampere Altra 64-bit cores. A complimentary public IPv4 address is provisioned by default.

The Ampere Altra arm64 design offers favorable qualitative efficiency, providing consistent core performance without the overhead of shared hyperthreading resources. The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio accommodates large working sets without wasting compute capacity. However, software environments must support the aarch64 instruction set, and the lack of local disk requires external volume attachments for persistent storage. Given this configuration, the server is suitable for in-memory caching solutions such as Redis or Memcached, memory-intensive data processing pipelines, web backend microservices, and native Arm build or CI/CD systems.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.16-128 is an Arm-based virtual machine configured with 16 dedicated physical cores and 128 GB of system memory. Powered by Ampere Altra processors running at a sustained 3.0 GHz clock rate, the instance assigns one hardware thread per vCPU, avoiding resource contention typical of simultaneous multithreading. With an 8 GB memory-to-core ratio, this profile is geared toward memory-heavy applications. The server includes no local NVMe storage and no discrete GPU acceleration, requiring reliance on remote block storage for non-volatile data persistence. The single-threaded physical core execution model provides predictable per-thread performance across all 16 cores. Consequently, the instance is technically aligned with workloads such as in-memory databases, Redis caches, large-scale multi-threaded Arm development builds, data analytics, and high-concurrency microservice application tiers.
